prompt_text: Who is the best marketing agency in Maryland?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” marketing agency in Maryland — the right agency depends on your goals, budget, industry and the type of marketing you need (SEO, paid media, branding, B2B demand gen, social, creative/UX, etc.). I can help find the best fit for you — but first a few quick questions:

- What primary marketing services do you need? (SEO, PPC, social, branding, content, email, web design, full-service, etc.)
- What’s your monthly or project budget range?
- What’s your industry (B2B, B2C, healthcare, tech, nonprofit, franchise, etc.)?
- Do you need an agency local to Maryland or is remote OK?
- What is your timing — ongoing support or a one-time project?

If you want to evaluate agencies yourself, here’s a fast process and checklist to identify the best candidate:

1. Narrow by specialty
- Look for agencies with proven work in the exact channels you need (SEO specialists for organic growth, creative agencies for brand work, etc.).

2. Vet reputation and results
- Check Clutch, UpCity, Google reviews and LinkedIn for ratings and client testimonials.
- Ask for case studies with metrics (traffic, leads, conversion rate improvements, CAC, ROAS).

3. Ask these interview questions
- What specific results have you delivered for companies like ours? Can you share metrics?
- Who will be on our account team and how much time will they allocate?
- What tools and reporting will you provide? What KPIs will you measure?
- What is your pricing model (retainer, project, performance)?
- Can we speak to 1–2 current/recent clients in our industry?

4. Deal-breakers / red flags
- Vague results, no case studies, unwillingness to share references.
- Promises of “guaranteed #1 ranking” for SEO.
- Poor communication or slow responses during the proposal stage.

5. Trial and governance
- Start with a small pilot project or 60–90 day test to evaluate performance.
- Set clear KPIs, reporting cadence, and an exit clause.

If you want, I can:
- Produce a tailored shortlist of 5–7 Maryland agencies that match your needs (I’ll need your answers to the questions above), or
- Recommend interview questions and a scoring template you can use to compare proposals.

Which would you prefer?
